subject: Some variance-covariance matrix elements were NA, possible numerical problems....

messages.author: d194c7e3cac8dcfe
messages.subject: Some variance-covariance matrix elements were NA, possible numerical problems....
parts:
Dear list,

I have been creating detection functions for right whales using behavior, size, and Beaufort as covariates.  All of my right whale sightings have a behavior code, size, and Beaufort.  My model that includes behavior and size together gives me the following error…

“Some variance-covariance matrix elements were NA, possible numerical problems; only estimating detection function.”


The only NA’s in the size and behavior column are for tracklines in which there were no sightings. 


It has no problem with the model that includes behavior, size, and Beaufort (which was curious to me). 

 

Any ideas?

Thanks!

~Laura Ganley

PhD student

University of Massachusetts, Boston

Laura

Fitting covariates to detection functions is difficult.  There are a number of "tricks" involved in doing so.  The section of the Users Guide entitled "MCDS analysis guidelines" is something you should consult.  Before having Distance try to fit models, do some exploratory analysis to see if covariates are correlated (they may be so by coincidence).  You may also need to choose starting values to avoid some of the numerical problems you describe.

Ask yourself how much your estimates of abundance are influenced by covariates included.
